title: Daniel 2: the statue and the stone
opening_question: Nebuchadnezzar dreamed of a great image of gold, silver, brass, iron and clay, and a stone cut out without hands. What did the dream show, and whose kingdom stands for ever?

steps.question: What did the king demand of the wise men, and why could they not do it?

facts.text: Where the Chaldeans answer the king "in Syriack" (Daniel 2:4), the book itself switches from Hebrew to Aramaic, and stays in Aramaic through Daniel 7.
The king asked for the dream itself, not only its meaning: "tell me the dream, and I shall know that ye can shew me the interpretation thereof".

steps.question: Whom did Daniel go to first, and what did God reveal to him in a night vision?

facts.text: The word for "secret" is raz. Strong's gives it as "a mystery".

steps.question: What was the great image made of, and what happened to it when the stone struck it?

facts.text: The word for "image" is tselem. Strong's gives it as "an idolatrous figure".
Head "of fine gold", breast and arms "of silver", belly and thighs "of brass", legs "of iron", feet "part of iron and part of clay".
"cut out" is gezar: "to quarry". The text does not say who cut the stone, only that it was "without hands".

steps.question: Which kingdoms do the metals stand for, and what kingdom shall never be destroyed?

facts.text: The word for "kingdom" is malku: "dominion". It is used for every kingdom of the image and for the kingdom the God of heaven sets up.
"brake in pieces" is deqaq: "to crumble or (transitively) crush".
Other verses on the kingdoms that fall and the reign that stands (the cross-references the TS2009 gives at verse 44).
